text: More than 2,500 years ago, a teacher called Confucius lived in the small state of Lu, in China.
He spent years travelling, looking for a ruler who would follow his ideas, but he did not find one.
src: Confucius (Kongzi, 551–479 BCE) / in the small state of Lu, in present-day Shandong
spending years travelling among the states, seeking a ruler who would put his ideas into practice. / He did not find one.

text: His students wrote down his sayings, which became a book called the Analects.
He taught care for others: “Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire.”
src: his students / who recorded his sayings and conversations; these were compiled over the following generations into the Analects
ren, humaneness or benevolence: the love and consideration for others / “Do not impose on others what you yourself do not desire.”

text: Confucius taught that a good society needs kind, thoughtful people who respect their parents and families.
Later, a thinker called Mencius taught that people are good by nature.
src: a good society rests on humane, cultivated people who honour their families / Filial piety, xiao, the respect and care owed to parents and ancestors
Mencius, in the 4th century BCE, who taught that human nature is good

text: He taught that anyone could become a good and wise person through learning.
For many centuries, men in China took hard tests on the Confucian books to become government officials.
src: he taught that anyone could become a junzi through education, whatever their birth
Officials were selected, increasingly from the Song dynasty onwards, through examinations on the Confucian classics / only a small fraction of candidates passed the highest degree

text: Emperors offered gifts at his home town of Qufu, where his family temple grew into a huge set of buildings.
His teaching spread to Korea, Japan and Vietnam.
src: Han emperors offered sacrifices at his home town of Qufu, where his family temple became a vast complex
the model of government in Korea, Japan and Vietnam

text: Reformers attacked it in the last century, but today its ideas of learning and family duty are shared by hundreds of millions.
Ceremonies for Confucius are still held in Seoul, and in Taiwan his birthday is celebrated as Teachers' Day.
src: Attacked as a cause of backwardness in the 20th century / its values of family, learning and ritual are shared by hundreds of millions across East Asia
Ceremonies to Confucius are still held at Qufu and at the shrine of Confucius in Seoul, and Confucius’s birthday is celebrated as Teachers’ Day in Taiwan
